text:
Tristan Luneau has a point in seven straight games, and the Ducks have won five of their last six. Those two facts are related. He has 10 points in his last ten games, more than double the 4.4 we'd expect at his ice time, and the Ducks have scored when he's out there: they take 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him, a whopping 18 points better than without him.

The caveat is the shooting. He has 3 goals on 1.48 expected and is shooting 14.3% against a range we'd put between 5% and 10% for a defenseman like him. That won't hold. The playmaking might. He's running power-play time (3 power-play points) and logging 20 minutes a night at 22.

This is a 2022 second-round pick who played 14 NHL games before this season and spent his junior career in Gatineau putting up 83 points in his final year. Our projection puts him around 49 points for the season, which feels high to us, but less crazy than it did a month ago. The thing to watch is whether the on-ice share holds once the goals cool. If it does, Anaheim has found a top-four defenseman.
headline: Tristan Luneau has arrived in Anaheim
